comments: The Approve/Decline buttons on the Teams approval card point here.
TWO workflows, and the split is forced by the platform rather than by
taste. A Consumption Logic App Request trigger accepts exactly one HTTP
method: with none declared it accepts POST only, and a GET is rejected by
the runtime with TriggerRequestMethodNotValid before the workflow starts.
triggerOutputs() has no 'method' property either -- only headers, queries
and body. So a single workflow cannot render a page on GET and write on
POST, however it is written. An earlier version of this file tried, by
branching on toupper(triggerOutputs()['method']), and that expression can
never evaluate.
bi-triage-approval-confirm   GET  -> renders a confirmation page.
Holds no connection and has no
action that can write anything.
bi-triage-approval-callback  POST -> records the decision.
That preserves the property the design actually needs: a link in a Teams
message is fetched by preview generators, link scanners and prefetchers,
and every one of those issues GET. GET reaches a workflow with nothing to
change. An approval a link preview can grant is not an approval.
State lives in a Fabric SQL Database, which speaks TDS and has no REST
data plane, so the write uses the SQL managed connector authenticating as
the recording workflow's own system-assigned identity. No key and no
connection string appears anywhere in this deployment.
The write is a stored procedure call, never SQL built from the URL.
Everything in that URL is attacker-controllable: anyone holding the link
can edit it. Parameters cannot carry SQL.
Two guarantees live in the procedure, because a Logic App cannot hold a
transaction open across a read and a write:
* the row moves from unanswered to answered exactly once, so two
simultaneous clicks cannot overwrite each other;
* fingerprint and expiry are checked in the statement that writes.
The agent revalidates all of it independently before acting.

resources.comments: Managed-identity auth for the SQL connector lives in the 'oauthMI' parameter value set, whose only parameter is a token of type managedIdentity constrained to location 'logicapp'. The identity is therefore supplied by the workflow at run time and the connection holds no credential of its own. Server and database are given per action, not here.

Record_the_decision.description: One parameterised stored-procedure call. It refuses a request that is unknown, already answered, expired, or whose fingerprint does not match the link, and reports how many rows it changed.

inputs.body:
Decision recorded

@{coalesce(triggerOutputs()['queries']?['decision'], '')} — @{coalesce(triggerOutputs()['queries']?['request_id'], '')}

The agent picks this up on its next poll. You can close this tab.

Refuse.description: Zero rows changed. The request does not exist, was already answered, has expired, or the fingerprint does not match. All four are refusals, and none of them changed anything.

inputs.body:
Not recorded

This request was already answered, has expired, or the link does not match it. Nothing was changed.

Could_not_reach_the_database.description: A write that did not happen must never render as a decision. Failing loudly is what stops somebody closing the tab believing they approved something.

inputs.body:
Not recorded

The decision store could not be reached, so nothing was written. Answer from the CLI with bi-triage approve, or try again.

resources.comments: The confirmation workflow. This is what the card's Action.OpenUrl link points at, so it is what preview generators and link scanners will fetch. It holds no connection and has no ApiConnection action, so it cannot change anything however many times it is replayed. The recording URL is injected at deploy time because a workflow cannot call listCallbackUrl() for a different workflow at run time.
resources.name: [parameters('confirmName')]

Ask_for_confirmation.description: Renders a page whose button POSTs to the recording workflow. Nothing has changed at this point, and nothing in this workflow is able to change anything.

inputs.body:
Confirm decision

You are about to record @{coalesce(triggerOutputs()['queries']?['decision'], '')} for request @{coalesce(triggerOutputs()['queries']?['request_id'], '')}.
